chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever's recitation is 'Indeed We have granted you al-Kawthar' in his obligatory and recommended prayers, Allah will cause him to drink from al-Kawthar on the Day of Resurrection, and his companion/angel will be with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) at the root of the tree of Tuba.

key_terms.أَصْلِ طُوبَى: The root/base of the Tree of Tuba in Paradise.
key_terms.إِنَّا أَعْطَيْنَاكَ الْكَوْثَرُ: The opening verse of Surah Al-Kawthar, referring to the divine gift of abundance.
key_terms.مُحَدَّثُهُ: His companion or the one who speaks to him (often interpreted as an angel or the Prophet himself in this context).
key_terms.مِنْ الْكَوْثَرِ: From the river of Kawthar in Paradise.

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Al-Kawthar in prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq links the consistent recitation of Surah Al-Kawthar in both obligatory and voluntary prayers to the spiritual privilege of having a divine companion (muhaddath) at the root of the Tree of Tuba, a concept deeply rooted in Shia eschatology. This narration underscores the Surah’s role not merely as a declaration of divine favor, but as a means of securing intimate proximity to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in the Hereafter.
